articleTitle: Short-Term Wind Power Forecasting Based on VMD-QPSO-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: The unpredictable and highly variable nature of wind power generation demands advanced predictive models to enhance the operational stability of power systems under non-stationary wind conditions. This study presents an innovative approach for short-term wind power prediction, ingeniously integrating Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), Quantum Particle Swarm Optimization (QPSO), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network into a cohesive forecasting methodology. Initially, VMD is applied to deconstruct wind power data into distinct sub-modes, thus reducing data complexity and facilitating more accurate analysis. The LSTM model is then fine-tuned using QPSO to refine its hyperparameters, thereby optimizing forecast performance. Each sub-mode is forecasted through a specialized LSTM model, and the collective forecasts are compounded to form the final prediction. Comparative analyses with conventional LSTM, PSO-enhanced LSTM, and QPSO-LSTM models reveal that our proposed VMD-QPSO-LSTM approach yields significantly higher accuracy in forecasting, highlighting its potential to efficiently navigate the uncertainties associated with wind power generation.

articleTitle: A Collaborative Filtering Algorithm for Improving Similarity Based on Probability Weighted Association Rules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: The sparsity of data and the accuracy of similarity calculation have always been the focus of collaborative filtering algorithms. To address this issue, a collaborative filtering algorithm PWAR-CF (The combination of probability weighted association rules in collaborative filtering) which combines probability weighted association rules is proposed. The algorithm employs probability-based weighted association rules to extract the potential correlation among users, and obtains the weighted confidence between users. According to the weighted confidence, the predictive score matrix is used to fill the original score matrix to alleviate the problem of sparse data. The weighted confidence is fused with the Person correlation coefficient, and enhanced similarity formula is utilized to compute the updated similarity between users. Finally, according to the prediction scoring formula, recommendations are generated for users. The Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) indexes are used on MovieLens data sets to prove that the proposed algorithm effectively alleviates the problems of data sparsity and similarity calculation accuracy, and has better recommendation quality than traditional algorithms.

articleTitle: A Method for Calculating the Over-the-Top Tracking Direction of a Small Cross-Beam Airborne Satellite Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: The main task of the airborne satellite antenna is to calculate the pointing angle of the antenna in real time based on the target satellite information and the aircraft's position and attitude data, and to control the antenna to quickly align with the satellite and track it. When the elevation angle of the aircraft is high and the circling attitude is large, the antenna may enter the state of overshooting tracking. The commonly used A-E frame satellite antenna cannot track at high elevation angles, and the cross-axis design of the A-E-C frame airborne satellite antenna has a limited range of motion due to envelope and weight constraints. The commonly used pointing calculation method for the A-E-C frame may face limitations due to the small range of motion of the cross-axis, which cannot meet the tracking and communication requirements. This paper discusses the reasons why the commonly used tracking pointing calculation method for the A-E frame airborne antenna cannot achieve high elevation angle tracking when the aircraft is in a large attitude circling. And then it analyzes the problems faced by the commonly used tracking pointing calculation method under the premise of a small cross-axis for the A-E-C frame. Subsequently, a new tracking pointing calculation method based on the A-E-C small cross-axis frame is proposed, which can significantly improve the overshooting tracking performance of the airborne satellite antenna.

articleTitle: Adaptive Discrete-Time Integral Sliding Mode Control for Motion Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: An adaptive discrete-time integral sliding mode control is developed for motion control systems. First, an adaptive reaching law is designed to eliminate the chattering, while retaining the robustness against many kinds of disturbances. Then, a modified two-step delayed method is developed to estimate the disturbance. Finally, the proposed control method is applied to a practical permanent-magnet synchronous motor system.

articleTitle: A model for capacitive grating sensors applied in simulation design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: The capacitive grating sensors with dedicated integrated chips are widely used in a variety of measurement devices, and the design has a significant impact on the overall system performance of the sensor under the same materials and processes. This article analyzes the structural principles and working characteristics of the capacitive grating sensor. And for the problem that the chip input signal cannot be directly given by the chip input signal in the simulation design process, a segmented transmission function of the capacitor and displacement is designed. We need to use the Verilog-A language to model the capacitive grating sensor, and simulate the correctness of the model on the Cadence Spectre, which improves the simulation speed and makes the simulation and practice more fit.

articleTitle: Classification Method of Motion Image EEG Signals Based on LMD-FBCSP and IGASVM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that traditional signal analysis methods cannot deal with nonlinear and non-stationary EEG signals effectively, which leads to inaccurate feature extraction and poor classification effect, this paper proposes an EEG signal classification method based on Local Mean Decomposition (LMD), Filter Bank Common Space Pattern (FBCSP) and Improved Genetic Algorithm (IGA) to optimize Support Vector Machine (SVM). By means of LMD, the pre-processed EEG signals are adaptive divided into multiple product functions (PF) and a residual quantity, from which the most discriminant PF components are selected to form a matrix, and the corresponding spatial features are extracted using the FBCSP. The features containing the largest amount of information are selected and combined into the feature matrix, which is sent to the IGA optimized SVM for classification, and the average classification accuracy is 91.0714%. The results show that the method has certain practicability and reliability.

articleTitle: A Service Matching Index Based Protection Path Selection Strategy in Multi-Dimensional Elastic Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of computer and communication technologies, the volume of network services has expanded dramatically, alongside increasingly diversified service demands. Consequently, traditional multi-dimensional elastic optical networks (MD-EONs) must enhance their survivability to ensure uninterrupted service in the face of various network challenges and disruptions. This paper proposes an MD-EON protection path selection method based on a service matching index (SMI). With SMI, we assess the situations of complete and incomplete matching between service-protected and idle spectrum fragments on fiber cores, with a preference for complete matches to reduce spectrum fragmentation. Additionally, based on the service protection requirement level, we dynamically adjust the calculation method of the SMI. The variable nature of spectrum occupancy on fiber cores introduces more flexible spectrum allocation, improving the selection of the core for protection paths and thus network reliability. Simulation results validate the performance of the proposed algorithm in terms of blocking probability and spectrum utilization. Compared to contrastive algorithms, it significantly improves network resource utilization and reduces service blocking probability.

articleTitle: Research on a Decomposition Method for Remote Sensing Satellite Monitoring Tasks in Striped Regions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: In response to the large coverage range of strip area monitoring and the limited image width of satellite borne remote sensors, each observation activity can only cover a local area of the target, and remote sensors need to perform multiple observation activities to fully cover the target, and a task decomposition method for strip area monitoring is studied. Taking into account factors such as satellite orbit, satellite borne remote sensor observation range, remote sensor imaging mode, visible time window, and regional target geographic location, reasonable and effective segmentation of strip area targets is carried out to provide input for satellite collaborative planning.

articleTitle: Robust Node Embedding Based on Subspace Attribute Complement Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have been proven to be powerful tools for graph analysis. However, despite their success, existing GNNs are often sensitive to the quality of the input graph. Real-world graphs are typically noisy, often represented topologically as containing some edges irrelevant to the task or missing some edges, which can lead to sub-optimal generalization performance of the learned GNNs models. To address this issue, we introduce a robust node representation algorithm for attribute networks based on the concept of subspace (STSAI) algorithm. Adequate experiments were also done on the real-world dataset to verify the validity of this work.

articleTitle: Research on Quality Prediction of Airborne Software Based on Neural Network Optimized by Ant Colony Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: This study addresses the issue of software quality prediction for airborne systems and proposes an optimization method for Backpropagation Neural Network (BPNN) based on Ant Colony Algorithm, referred to as SQP-ACO-BPNN. With the advancement of neural network technology, this method aims to overcome the challenges in selecting the network structure and initial connection parameters in traditional software quality prediction models. By employing the Ant Colony Algorithm to optimize the neural network structure, initial connection weights, and thresholds, the model is capable of more accurately fitting the relationship between software features and quality. Experimental results demonstrate that SQP-ACO-BPNN significantly improves accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score compared to the non-optimized BPNN, providing a more reliable model for software quality prediction. Future research directions include optimizing Ant Colony Algorithm parameters, incorporating other metaheuristic algorithms and deep learning techniques, adjusting neural network structures, and applying the method in different domains to advance research and practical applications in software engineering quality prediction.

articleTitle: Design and Research of a DC Charging Station Measurement and Monitoring System for Electric Vehicles Based on DC Measurement Chips
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: This paper designs a DC charging station measurement and monitoring system for electric vehicles based on DC metering chips, integrating DC meters and billing control units, and integrating DC meters, splitters, and billing control units. Implementing an integrated design approach, the system comprises a Metering Module and a Billing Control Module. The Metering Module is tasked with gathering and quantifying the charger's energy consumption. It transmits the recorded voltage, current, and energy data to the Billing Control Module. The Billing Control Module, in turn, engages with users and performs various functions including fee payment, charging mode selection, and control of the charging device.

articleTitle: Study of Two Novel Ultra-Low Specific On-Resistance 4H-SiC SGT MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: SiC MOSFET has been commercialized for industrial and automotive applications for many years. However, there is a contradictory relation between the specific resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}_{\text{on,sp}}$</tex> and breakdown voltage BV for both MOSFET. There are many ways to get better trade-off relationship, such as SJ structures and SGT structures. In this paper, a SGT MOSFET with novel structure was introduced, which showed its static characteristics and dynamic characteristics in contrast with VDMOS and Trench MOS. Due to the reduced temperature dependence, the proposed SGT MOSFET has better static performances, particularly at high temperatures. The proposed SGT devices showed ultra-low Ron, sp, the Ron, sp of Side P Structure is 0.89 mΩ*cm2 at 25 °C and 1.82 mΩ*cm2 at 175 °C, the Ron, sp of Bottom P Structure is 0.98 mΩ*cm2 at 25 °C and 2.12 mΩ*cm2 at 175 °C. In addition, owing to the super-junction structure's poor performance in UIS tests, the avalanche tolerance of the novel structures was investigated and the result is that the avalanche tolerance of the two proposed structures is in between that of VDMOS and Trench MOS.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Network for Lip Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: Visual speech recognition (VSR) is also known as lip recognition. Recently, it has been widely explored due to the development of deep learning. Lip recognition is a discrimination issue, where the information provided by the delicate movement of the lips is most remarkable of all. This places a higher demand on the model's ability to extract features of minor variation around the lips. In this paper, a three-dimensional convolutional network (3D CNN) multi-branch feature fusion network is proposed for extracting spatiotemporal featuresof continuous images. The features of multi-branch feature fusion network are utilized to fully extract partial and general characteristics from sequential imagery and further enhance the feature information to deliver more accurate function info to the back-end classification network. The excellence of quite a few methods requires the support of huge volume of data, and in favor of test the effect of small-scale data sets. This experimentis conducted using the Oulu Vs2dataset to obtain exciting experimental results. After 20 iterations of the experiment, the maximum accuracy absolutely improves by 0.8% and the average accuracy improves by 1%.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Analysis and Suggestions for Equalizing Capacitors of 500kV HGIS Circuit Breakers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: The article introduces the classification of ultra-high voltage switches and elaborates on the structure and advantages of gas insulated metal fully enclosed switchgear. In response to a fault in a 500kV gas insulated metal fully enclosed switchgear, diagnostic tests were conducted on the circuit breaker. Through onsite testing and factory disassembly analysis, the cause of the circuit breaker fault was identified, and corresponding technical and supervisory suggestions were proposed based on the actual operation situation in the network.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Detection of Missing Wind Turbine Tower Nuts
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: The integrity of the tower screws and nuts of wind turbines, a key component of renewable energy technologies, is critical to the stability and safe operation of the entire structure. Traditional inspection methods rely on manual visual inspection, which is not only time-consuming and labour intensive, but also susceptible to subjective factors and environmental conditions. In this study, a deep learning approach, based on a target detection algorithm model, is able to accurately locate missing nuts on wind turbine towers by training a homemade dataset training and analysing it, which improves the maintenance efficiency and safety of wind turbine equipment.
